content.comment_body: Hello, I'm experiencing an issue when trying to download a web project to my [product_name]. Initially, I was able to upload projects successfully, but after making some changes I received the error: "Download Failed! Invalid name in SD Card." I thought the SD card might be faulty, so I replaced it, but the problem persisted. I also tried creating a new web project from scratch, but still encountered the same error. Hardware: [article_no]. Web editor: [version_no]. Does anyone know what might cause this?
Could you please upload your [product_name] web project and program so we can take a closer look?

I haven't encountered issues transferring the [product_name] web project to [product_name]. Everything runs smoothly. I've attached a screenshot of the webserver. However, it looks like you chose the wrong block format in the editor. For integer values, you should use "Signed" instead of "Unsigned".
Hello, It actually worked before even with the "Unsigned" setting, but suddenly I started getting this error. So, you're not sure why this happens?
I've made the changes but still see the "Download failed! Invalid name in SD Card" error. What could this indicate?

The block format settings shouldn't be the issue, as incorrect settings would just show incorrect values. I suspect there could be a problem with your SD card or the SD slot itself. What does the diagnostics menu display? [product_name] main menu > diagnostics > hardware > SD card
Hi, Diagnostics show no issues with the SD card.
In that case, I'm out of ideas. On my [product_name], everything works as expected without problems. Maybe it's worth submitting a support request.
Thanks for your help. I've submitted a service request.

Hi, I discovered the root of the error when downloading a web project to my [product_name]. Changing the name of the web project to match the LSC allowed the download to work correctly. Everything is now functioning. My conclusion: you cannot change the name of the web project once it's been downloaded to the [product_name].

I'm not sure I understand. I transferred the projects you provided ([product_name] web project = Jacuzzi, LSC = WP control) to my [product_name] with no problems. Then I renamed the web project from Jacuzzi to WP control and uploaded it successfully. Renaming it back was also easy and caused no issues during upload.

Hello? The service request didn't lead to a solution; support couldn't identify the cause, so I ran additional tests. After changing the web project name from 'jacuzzi' to 'WP control', which matches the LSC project name, I was able to download and run the web project again. It seems this is related to the naming convention. The issue started after I changed the name and stopped once I made both names the same. It appears that the device memory checks the web project name, even when starting a new project. Thanks for your help and testing!

I don't think that's the case, since my own tests didn't show that behavior. I tested on your projects and had no issues. The web project and [product_name] file names don't have to be identical; they can differ.

I understand your position, but that's my testing result and it's now working for me. My only hypothesis is that some internal memory in the device links to the web project name. I plan to run more tests next week to see if I can reproduce the error and will update everyone.

analysis.insight_summary: A user faces a recurring error message ('Download Failed! Invalid name in SD Card') when attempting to download a web project using the [product_name] web editor to their hardware, despite replacing the SD card and recreating the project. Another community member confirms successful uploads on their own setup, suggesting that the issue is specific to the user's device or configuration. The error remains unresolved even after troubleshooting, resulting in frustration and a support request. Eventually, the user finds that aligning the project name with a corresponding file allows the download to succeed, prompting discussion over naming conventions and internal memory mechanisms.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects reliable project downloads from the [product_name] web editor to the hardware SD card, without encountering persistent errors. Clear diagnostics and feedback are also expected to help determine any file naming or SD card compatibility issues.
